the forespore wall of S. pombe is composed of two membranes, the inner one of which becomes the spore plamsalemma and the other, if it persists becomes the limiting membrane of the forespore.
the forespore membranes emerge at the beginning of Meiosis II, and that they are resolved into two separate membrane systems during the formation of the spore walls.
the spore membrane emerges from the cytoplasmic membrane and the spore wall is deposited between the two membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
ultrastructural changes of the S. pombe during ascospore maturation.
ultrastructural changes of S. pombe during the formation of ascospore and the process of ascospore formation in this organism.
the ultrastructural changes of fission yeast (S. pombe) during the process of ascosporogenesis and the mechanism of ascospore formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fission yeast ascosporogenesis resembles the ascospore formation of the higher fungi in the following respects: the formation of two nuclei during meiosis I, the enclosure of the meiotic nuclei and other cytoplamsic organelles in forespore membrane, the resolution of forespore membrane into two separate membranes, the deposition of the spore walls in the space between two membranes.
the fission yeast, S.pombe, is similar to the budding yeast, S.cerevisiae, in the process of ascospore formation, but differs in the process of nuclear division during meiosis.
the spore wall is formed by the fusion of the outer forespore membrane with the inner forespore membrane and the subsequent deposition of the spore-wall materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fission yeast, S. pombe, undergoes a meiosis similar to that in the budding yeast, S. cerevisiae, except that meiosis occurs without fragmentation.
the fission yeast, S. pombe, is a good material for studying the ascosporogenetic process and the ultrastructure of the ascosphere.
the forespore membranes of S. pombe are resolved into two separate ones, the spore plamalemma and a limiting membrane of spore wall.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meiosis in fission yeast is a very different process from meiosis in other organisms, such as yeast and humans.
there is a single nuclear envelope during the entire meiotic process and that there are no nuclear membrane fragments.
the forespore wall membrane of the fission yeasts is formed by the fusion of two separate membranes.
